string.name: setup_intro
string.description: Introduction on the first-launch screen, which explains what Crumbles collects, where the data goes and what the app never does. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Crumbles records security and network activity on this phone so that it can be checked for signs of attack. Read what it collects, where it goes and what it never does before you continue.

string.name: setup_collected_heading
string.description: Heading of the section of the first-launch screen that lists the data Crumbles collects. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: What Crumbles collects

string.name: setup_collected_body
string.description: Bulleted list, on the first-launch screen, of the data Crumbles collects. DNS is the technical name of the system that looks up server addresses. USB debugging is the name of an Android developer setting. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: • Security events that Android records, such as apps starting, screen unlock attempts, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connections, and commands sent over USB debugging.\n• While network logging is on, the DNS lookups and connections made by every app and by everyone using this phone. They show which servers were contacted and by which app, not what was sent.\n• The activity log: what is done in Crumbles and when, such as turning logging on or off, or changing the encryption key or the upload destination.

string.name: setup_destination_heading
string.description: Heading of the section of the first-launch screen that explains where the collected data goes. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Where it goes

string.name: setup_destination_body
string.description: Explanation, on the first-launch screen, of how the collected logs are protected and where they are uploaded. WebDAV is the technical name of a file server protocol. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Crumbles encrypts logs on this phone with the active encryption key, so only the holder of the matching private key can read them. It uploads the encrypted batches to the folder or WebDAV server you choose.

string.name: setup_never_heading
string.description: Heading of the section of the first-launch screen that lists what Crumbles never does. Each item of the list that follows completes the sentence of this heading. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: What Crumbles never does

string.name: setup_never_body
string.description: Bulleted list, on the first-launch screen, of what Crumbles never does. Each item completes the heading 'What Crumbles never does'. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string:
• Store or upload security or network logs unencrypted.
• Send data anywhere other than the destination you choose. There is no telemetry and no analytics.
• Back up its data to the cloud or copy it to another device.
• Accept connections from the network.
• Read your messages, contacts, call history, photos or files.

string.description: Message of the server identity dialog. %1$s is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server's public key, as lines of colon-separated hexadecimal bytes. Uploads go only to a server that presents this key once the user saves. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Ask the server\'s operator for the fingerprint of its key, and save only if it matches this one. If it does not, someone may be intercepting the connection.\n\n%1$s

string.name: webdav_server_key_confirm_button
string.description: Button of the server identity dialog that saves the WebDAV settings, pinned to the key whose fingerprint the dialog shows. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Save

string.name: webdav_server_key_unreadable
string.description: Message of the server identity dialog when the WebDAV server's key cannot be read, because the server cannot be reached or its certificate is not trusted. Nothing is saved. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Could not verify the server\'s identity, so nothing was saved. Check the URL and network connection.

string.name: decrypt_logs_prompt_title
string.description: Title of the prompt asking the user to authenticate before the selected log files are decrypted. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: Decrypt log files

string.name: decrypt_logs_prompt_subtitle
string.description: Subtitle of the prompt asking the user to authenticate before log files are decrypted. It tells how many of the selected log files this one authentication decrypts. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE] [ICU SYNTAX]

resources.string: {count, plural, =1 {1 log file} other {# log files}}

string.name: decrypt_logs_separate_prompt_description
string.description: Text of the prompt asking the user to authenticate before decrypting the selected log files that cannot share one authentication with the others, such as files saved by an older version of the app. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

resources.string: These log files need their own authentication.

string.name: decrypt_logs_own_prompt_description
string.description: Text of the prompt asking the user to authenticate before decrypting one selected log file that needs an authentication of its own. count is how many more of the selected files need one after this file. Cancelling the prompt skips this file and those files. [CHAR LIMIT=NONE] [ICU SYNTAX]

resources.string: {count, plural, =0 {This log file needs its own authentication. Cancel to skip it.} =1 {This log file needs its own authentication. Cancel to skip it and # more file.} other {This log file needs its own authentication. Cancel to skip it and # more files.}}

plurals.name: btn_wipe_kept_copies_label
plurals.description: Label on the main screen for the button that deletes uploaded log copies still kept on this phone while the storage app syncs them, after the user confirms the screen lock. %d is the number of kept copies (for example 2). [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]

string.name: btn_wipe_kept_copies_and_pending_label
string.description: Label on the main screen for the button that deletes, after the user confirms the screen lock, both the uploaded log copies kept on this phone while the storage app syncs them and the log batches not uploaded yet, which are lost. kept is the number of kept copies and pending the number of batches not uploaded (for example 2). [CHAR LIMIT=NONE] [ICU SYNTAX]

resources.string: Wipe anyway ({kept, plural, =1 {# kept copy} other {# kept copies}}, {pending, plural, =1 {# batch not uploaded} other {# batches not uploaded}})

plurals.name: label_saf_kept_copies
plurals.description: Label on the main screen below the Wipe anyway button explaining that uploaded log copies stay on this device until Google Drive syncs them. Drive is the product name for Google Drive, not a generic term. %d is the number of kept copies (for example 2). [CHAR LIMIT=NONE]
plurals.item: %d uploaded copy stays on this device until Drive syncs it.
%d uploaded copies stay on this device until Drive syncs them.
